pred_ddx.label: Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricular Septum

Tricuspid Atresia: The presence of a hypoplastic left ventricle, severely reduced mitral valve orifice, and two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle are consistent with tricuspid atresia.
Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricula: The severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, along with the presence of an interatrial defect and interventricular defect, could also suggest pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum, although the presence of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle makes this less likely.
